3:00|
4:19|Return NotImplemented, not False, upon rich comparison with unknown type
5:46|Comparison methods should ideally return ``NotImplemented`` when unable to make sense of the arguments. 6:00|

8:4f|```python
9:60|class Foo():
10:b1|    def __eq__(self, other):
11:b1|        if isinstance(other, sympy.Basic):  # Or something else that makes sense
12:aa|            return self._coefficient == other  # Or something else that makes sense
13:87|        ...
14:cd|```
15:e4|Currently, this leads to an unsymmetric equivalence relation. For an instance ``f`` of ``Foo`` and a sympy object ``s``, one may end up in situations where ``f == s`` is True (because ``Foo.__eq__`` was invoked), while ``s == f`` is False (because ``sympy.Basic.__eq__`` was invoked, and didn't understand the type of ``f``). If ``sympy.Basic.__eq__`` instead returned ``NotImplemented``, the statement ``s == f`` would delegate to ``Foo.__eq__``, thus maintaining a symmetric relation. The other rich comparison methods, ``__lt__``, ``__ge__``, and so on, behave similarly.

## Task
TASK.md asked for the minimal correct fix to sympy issue #13091: rich comparisons with unknown types must return `NotImplemented`, not `False`, so Python delegates to the other object's reflected method.

## Cause
In `sympy/core/basic.py`, `Basic.__eq__` caught `SympifyError` and returned `False` (line 316), so `s == f` was hard-`False` even when `Foo.__eq__` understood sympy objects — an unsymmetric relation. Additionally, `Basic.__ne__` did `return not self.__eq__(other)`, which would have turned a `NotImplemented` return into `False` (`not NotImplemented` is `False`) and silently corrupted internal `!=` logic (confirmed by a `DeprecationWarning: NotImplemented should not be used in a boolean context` and by `test_equals` returning `None` from `simplify`/`is_constant`).

## Fix — `sympy/core/basic.py`, 2 lines (working tree, not committed)
- Line 316: `return False    # sympy != other` → `return NotImplemented    # sympy != other`
- Line 332: `return not self.__eq__(other)` → `return not self == other` (same form modern sympy uses, so the fallback is handled by the interpreter)

No other comparison sites needed changes: `Expr.__lt__/__le__/__gt__/__ge__` already raise `TypeError` on unsympifiable operands by design (documented behavior), and `__lt__`/`__gt__` on `BasicMeta` compare classes only.
